text: #383 applies D-0260's principle, that what isn't proved is never called proved, and D-0264's refusal before Nagini runs, to what a file marked # +nagini imports. The pinned Nagini reads the modules a marked file imports and takes their contracts without proving their bodies. In its runs, a core proved fdiv(7, -2) == -3, where Python gives -4, through an unmarked helper whose contract uses //; a core verified through a helper whose body breaks its own contract, which Nagini rejects run on that helper alone; a stub helper.pyi beside a marked helper.py stood in for it; and a plain json.py in the package stood in for the standard library's json. So before Nagini runs, the gate reads every import a marked file holds, wherever it stands, in a function, a branch or a try as at the top, and refuses one of a module its package holds unless that module is another marked file the gate proves in the same run, imported by that file's own name, as import helper or from helper import f. Refused: a plain module and a test, which the gate never proves; a stub, a stub package or a directory, which Nagini would read in the module's place; a relative import and the package by its own name, which the pinned Nagini can't resolve, since it proves each marked file as a top-level module of its own; and a marked file the gate refuses, and so every proof on the way to it. The arithmetic rule holds for the marked file a core imports as for any marked file. Imports of the standard library, of nagini_contracts and of what the package doesn't hold are unaffected, and a top-level name the standard library or nagini_contracts provides is theirs whatever the package holds, since that is the module Python loads. A refusal fails the code check, as the arithmetic rule's does, with an error on each line it refuses, and the refused file's functions are named as ones Nagini never saw. Nagini then proves each marked file in a directory of its own, holding only that file and the marked files it imports, with the bytes the gate read, so it can read no other module of the project. A core that imports another marked core proves both, and the receipt counts both; when Nagini doesn't prove the one a core imports, the code check fails, and the gate says the core's proof rests on contracts Nagini didn't prove. An in-place proof can't reach a sibling's contracts this way: its verifier input copies only the function and its module's imports of Nagini's contracts and typing, __future__ imports and literal constants, binds every other name only to a trusted contract's abstraction in a module the gate writes, and runs in a directory holding only the input's files, so a sibling's own contract never reaches Nagini, and what an in-place proof may do is unchanged. Today's three cores import nothing of their package, and pass.
